intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM — collect luggage, pick up any pre-booked rental car or take TheBus (Oahu's public transit, ~$3/ride) to your accommodation. Check in or store luggage at your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach (free entry) — relax on the sand, swim in the warm Pacific, and get your bearings. Walk the Kalakaua Avenue strip to scout affordable dining options and pick up snacks at ABC Stores.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous free Waikiki sunset from the beach, then stroll to Kuhio Beach Hula Show (free, held nightly near the Kuhio Beach Torch Lighting). Grab a budget dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In near Waikiki — local plate lunches from $10-$13, a beloved Hawaii institution
meals.dinner: Marugame Udon in Waikiki — fresh udon bowls from $8-$12, quick and filling

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the midday arrival. Use TheBus Route 20 or 42 from the airport to Waikiki to save on taxi/rideshare costs (~$3 vs $35+). Pick up a reusable water bottle — staying hydrated is key in Hawaii's humidity.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike up Diamond Head State Monument (opens 6 AM, $5/person entry). The 1.6-mile round-trip trail rewards you with panoramic views of Waikiki and the coastline. Arrive early to beat crowds and heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for snorkeling (entry $25/adult, free for Hawaii residents and children under 13). Book online in advance as spots are limited. Rent snorkel gear on-site (~$15) and explore the stunning reef teeming with sea turtles and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or bus along the scenic Kalanianaole Highway back toward Waikiki. Stop at Kaimana Beach (quieter and free) for a relaxed evening swim before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leonard's Bakery — famous malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from $1.50 each, a must-try local treat
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a nearby grocery store (Times Supermarket or Foodland) — sandwiches, fruit, and drinks for under $10/person
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood — poke bowls from $12-$16, one of Honolulu's most beloved local spots

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations must be made online at least a day in advance. August weather may bring occasional afternoon showers (176mm monthly average) — carry a light rain jacket. Sunscreen is required at Hanauma Bay; use reef-safe sunscreen only.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic Iolani Palace (self-guided audio tour ~$20/adult, $6/child) — the only royal palace on US soil. Afterward, walk through the nearby Hawaii State Capitol grounds and Kawaiahao Church, both free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Chinatown Honolulu — browse the open-air markets, art galleries, and cultural shops. Stop at Oahu Market for fresh tropical fruits and local snacks at very low prices. Walk to the nearby Foster Botanical Garden (entry $5/adult, free for children under 13).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park (free) for a sunset walk along the 1.5-mile beach. Then browse Ala Moana Center's food court for affordable dinner options.

meals.breakfast: Café in Chinatown or a local bakery — dim sum or pastries for $5-$8
meals.lunch: Chinatown's Oahu Market or Little Village Noodle House — noodle dishes from $10-$14
meals.dinner: Ala Moana Center Food Court — wide variety of local and Asian options from $8-$14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Chinatown is very walkable and budget-friendly. The Foster Botanical Garden is a hidden gem with massive ancient trees. Keep an eye on your belongings in busy market areas.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the North Shore of Oahu (about 1 hour from Waikiki). Stop at Waimea Bay Beach Park — a stunning, wide beach perfect for families. In August, the summer swells are calm, making it ideal for swimming and snorkeling (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along Kamehameha Highway to Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach Park (Banzai Pipeline). Walk the shoreline and enjoy the scenery. Stop at Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa town — a legendary North Shore treat ($4-$6).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Haleiwa town's shops and galleries before heading back to Waikiki. Stop at a roadside shrimp truck (Giovanni's or Romy's) for a classic North Shore dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a local diner near your hotel before departing — loco moco or eggs from $8-$12
meals.lunch: Matsumoto Shave Ice for a snack, plus packed snacks from the grocery store
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — garlic shrimp plates ~$15, a North Shore institution

day_by_day.notes: Renting a car for this day is highly recommended as TheBus to North Shore takes 2+ hours each way. Gas up at Costco (if you have a membership) for the cheapest fuel on the island. North Shore is about a 1-hour drive from Waikiki.

day_by_day.morning: Take an inter-island flight to the Big Island (Hawaii Island) — book budget flights on Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest in advance for $60-$100 each way. Arrive at Kona or Hilo airport and pick up a rental car (essential on the Big Island).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (entry $35/vehicle, valid for 7 days — great value for families). Begin exploring the Kilauea Visitor Center, watch the orientation film, and walk the Crater Rim Trail to see the Halemaumau Crater and active volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.evening: After dark, return to the Jaggar Museum overlook (or current designated viewing area) to witness the glowing lava lake — one of Hawaii's most spectacular free natural shows. The sight is most dramatic at night.

meals.breakfast: Airport grab-and-go or hotel breakfast before flying
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from a grocery store before entering the park — no food vendors inside
meals.dinner: Cafe Ohia in Volcano Village near the park — local comfort food from $12-$18

day_by_day.notes: Check the National Park Service website for current volcanic activity and any trail closures before visiting. Volcanic fumes (vog) can be strong — those with respiratory issues should bring masks. Temperatures near the volcano can be cooler (~16°C), so bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Continue exploring Hawaii Volcanoes National Park. Hike the Thurston Lava Tube (free with park entry) — a fascinating 500-year-old lava tube walk. Then drive Chain of Craters Road down to the coast to see ancient petroglyphs and hardened lava fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Punaluu Black Sand Beach (free) — one of Hawaii's most unique beaches with jet-black volcanic sand. Watch for endangered Hawaiian green sea turtles (honu) basking on the shore. Swimming is possible but check conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Hilo town on the east side of the island. Explore the charming downtown area, visit the Hilo Farmers Market (open daily, best on Wednesdays and Saturdays), and pick up fresh local produce and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Volcano Village local café — eggs and toast from $8-$10
meals.lunch: Picnic at Punaluu Black Sand Beach with groceries from a local store
meals.dinner: Cafe 100 in Hilo — famous for the original loco moco, plates from $5-$10, extremely budget-friendly

day_by_day.notes: Do NOT touch or disturb the sea turtles at Punaluu — it is illegal and carries heavy fines. The black sand gets very hot in the sun; wear sandals. Hilo receives more rainfall than Kona, so expect possible afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Rainbow Falls in Hilo (free) — a beautiful 80-foot waterfall best seen in the morning when rainbows form in the mist. Then drive to Akaka Falls State Park ($5/vehicle) for a short 0.4-mile loop trail through lush rainforest to two stunning waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive up the Saddle Road (Highway 200) toward Mauna Kea. Stop at the Mauna Kea Visitor Information Station at 9,200 feet elevation (free) for stunning views and stargazing information. Note: driving to the summit requires a 4WD vehicle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hilo for the evening. Walk along Hilo Bay and Coconut Island (free) for a peaceful sunset view. Browse the shops along Kamehameha Avenue.

meals.breakfast: Two Ladies Kitchen in Hilo — famous mochi and Japanese sweets, grab a light breakfast from $5-$8
meals.lunch: Puna Kai Farmers Market or a local plate lunch spot in Hilo — $10-$13
meals.dinner: Suisan Fish Market in Hilo — fresh poke by the pound (~$14/lb), eat at the picnic tables outside

day_by_day.notes: Bring warm layers for the Mauna Kea Visitor Station — temperatures drop significantly at 9,200 feet even in August. The stargazing at the visitor station (free, nightly weather permitting) is world-class and a wonderful family activity.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Kona side of the Big Island (about 2.5 hours from Hilo). Stop at South Point (Ka Lae) — the southernmost point in the United States — for dramatic coastal views and a short walk (free). Continue to Green Sand Beach (Papakolea) — a rare olivine green sand beach accessible by a 2.5-mile walk each way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kailua-Kona town. Explore the historic Ahu'ena Heiau (free) and the Hulihee Palace museum ($10/adult, $5/child). Walk along Ali'i Drive and browse the open-air shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset from the Kona waterfront. Watch for spinner dolphins in the bay. Explore the Kona Farmers Market for local crafts and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from Hilo grocery store for the road trip
meals.lunch: Island Lava Java in Kona — sandwiches and wraps from $10-$14 with ocean views
meals.dinner: Da Poke Shack in Kona — award-winning poke bowls from $13-$17, often ranked among Hawaii's best

day_by_day.notes: The walk to Green Sand Beach is 5 miles round trip on uneven terrain — wear sturdy shoes and bring plenty of water. Some locals offer ATV rides for ~$15/person if walking is not feasible for the family. Book your return inter-island flight to Oahu for Day 9 or 10 in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkel at Two Step (Honaunau Bay) near Pu'uhonua o Honaunau National Historical Park — one of the Big Island's best free snorkeling spots with abundant marine life and sea turtles. Arrive early for the best conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pu'uhonua o Honaunau National Historical Park (Place of Refuge) — entry $20/vehicle. Explore the ancient Hawaiian temple grounds, royal fishponds, and carved ki'i (wooden statues). A fascinating cultural and historical experience for families.
day_by_day.evening: Fly back to Oahu from Kona airport (book evening flight in advance). Return to your Waikiki accommodation. Relax and prepare for the final day.

meals.breakfast: Grab groceries from a Kona supermarket — fruit, yogurt, and snacks for a beach breakfast
meals.lunch: Kona Brewing Company — pizzas and local dishes from $12-$16, try the award-winning craft beers (adults) or root beer (kids)
meals.dinner: Airport or Waikiki food court upon return — keep it simple and budget-friendly, $10-$15

day_by_day.notes: Two Step has no lifeguard — supervise children closely. The snorkeling is in a marine sanctuary, so no touching coral or marine life. Confirm your return flight timing and allow extra time for car return and airport check-in on the Big Island.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Oahu — visit the Pearl Harbor National Memorial (free entry to grounds and USS Arizona Memorial, though timed passes must be reserved online in advance). A deeply moving and historically significant experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to Waikiki for last-minute beach time at Kuhio Beach (free). Rent a bodyboard (~$10/hour) for some family fun in the waves. Browse the International Market Place for affordable souvenirs — look for locally made items like macadamia nut products, Kona coffee, and Hawaiian quilts.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset at Waikiki Beach — a perfect farewell to Hawaii. Enjoy a special last dinner at a slightly nicer budget restaurant to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Eggs 'n Things in Waikiki — famous for pancakes with whipped cream, breakfast from $12-$16
meals.lunch: Musubi Cafe Iyasume — spam musubi and onigiri from $2-$5 each, a perfect light Hawaiian snack lunch
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki — slightly splurge-worthy farewell dinner with ocean views, fish tacos and burgers from $16-$22; happy hour (4-6 PM) offers great deals

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor timed entry passes are free but must be reserved well in advance at recreation.gov — they fill up quickly, especially in summer. Pack any checked luggage with souvenirs carefully, noting TSA rules on liquids (honey, jams). Allow at least 3 hours before your departure flight for airport check-in and security.

trip_options.title: Classic Hawaii Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 11:20 AM (Alaska Airlines). Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange ground transportation to hotel. Check in early if possible or store luggage at SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, head to nearby Knott's Berry Farm or explore Downtown Disney (both within 10-15 minutes) for a low-key family afternoon to shake off travel fatigue. Alternatively, relax at the hotel pool.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first-night dinner close to the hotel. Stroll Buena Park's restaurant row on Beach Blvd for a casual family meal.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport before or after landing
meals.lunch: Mrs. Knott's Chicken Dinner Restaurant (Buena Park) — classic comfort food, family-friendly, mid-range pricing
meals.dinner: Spaghettini Grill & Jazz (Seal Beach, ~15 min) or BJ's Restaurant & Brewhouse on Beach Blvd for hearty family-friendly meals around $15–25/person

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 11:20 AM arrival. Focus on rest and orientation. Confirm any Hawaii inter-island flight or activity bookings for upcoming days. Note: The hotel is in Buena Park, CA — Hawaii activities begin once you fly to the islands. Days 2–3 are transition/prep days before flying to Hawaii on Day 3.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Disneyland Resort or Knott's Berry Farm for a full family fun day — both are within 5–10 minutes of the hotel. Purchase tickets in advance online for savings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the theme park. Enjoy rides, shows, and character meet-and-greets suited for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel, pack bags for the Hawaii flight tomorrow. Enjoy a relaxed dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Hotel continental breakfast or IHOP on Beach Blvd (~5 min drive)
meals.lunch: In-park dining at Disneyland (Blue Bayou for a mid-range splurge ~$30/person) or Knott's Chicken-to-Go for budget-friendly option
meals.dinner: In-N-Out Burger (Buena Park, quick and affordable) or Lucille's Smokehouse BBQ on La Palma Ave for a heartier family dinner

day_by_day.notes: Book Disneyland tickets well in advance — August is peak season. Knott's Berry Farm is a more affordable alternative. Confirm Hawaii flight details and pack reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early checkout and drive to LAX or John Wayne Airport (SNA). Fly to Honolulu, Oahu (approximately 5.5-hour flight). Arrive mid-afternoon Hawaii time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into Oahu hotel (mid-range recommendation: Aqua Aloha Surf Waikiki or Aston Waikiki Beach Hotel, ~$180–220/night). Take a short orientation walk along Waikiki Beach to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Hawaii! Watch the sunset from Waikiki Beach, then explore Kalakaua Avenue for dinner and shopping.

meals.breakfast: Quick grab-and-go at hotel or airport before departure
meals.lunch: Airport or in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Marukame Udon (Waikiki) — iconic, affordable, and delicious; expect a short line. Under $15/person for the whole family

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii is 3 hours behind California time — the family may feel energized in the evening. Apply reef-safe sunscreen from day one. Pick up a 'Snorkel Bob's' rental reservation for Hanauma Bay tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — arrive early (7:00–7:30 AM) as the bay reaches capacity quickly and closes to new visitors by mid-morning. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel among hundreds of tropical fish in this stunning marine sanctuary. Entry fee ~$25/adult, children under 12 free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Koko Head Crater area for a scenic drive along the Kalanianaole Highway. Stop at Halona Blowhole Lookout and Sandy Beach for photos and a beach break (Sandy Beach has strong shore break — supervise children closely).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki. Enjoy a traditional Hawaiian lu'au experience — consider the Royal Hawaiian Hotel's Monday Lu'au (~$135/adult, $75/child) for an authentic, mid-range option.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or Cinnamon's Restaurant in Kailua (~$12–18/person) before heading to Hanauma Bay
meals.lunch: Packed snacks and water at Hanauma Bay (no food vendors inside), or stop at Zippy's on Kalanianaole Hwy on the way back
meals.dinner: Royal Hawaiian Lu'au (if booked) or Ono Seafood in Kaimuki for fresh poke bowls (~$12–15/person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online — book at least 2 days ahead. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Bring water shoes for rocky entry points. August weather averages 16.8°C overnight but daytime beach temps are warm (~28–30°C).

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — arrive at opening (noon for daytime activities, but the full-day package starts at 12:00 PM). The center is located in Laie on the North Shore (~1 hour from Waikiki). Explore six authentic Polynesian village exhibits: Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — participate in hands-on cultural activities like fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional dance lessons. Ride the canoe through the villages.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show (~7:30 PM), a world-class Polynesian performance. The Ambassador Package (~$120–160/adult, $80–110/child) includes dinner buffet and show.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Leonard's Bakery (Honolulu) for famous malasadas (~$2 each) on the drive north
meals.lunch: Included in Polynesian Cultural Center package (Gateway Buffet) or Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Kahuku (~$15/plate) nearby
meals.dinner: Included in PCC Ambassador Package buffet dinner before the evening show

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets online in advance — August is peak season. The drive to Laie takes about 1 hour; consider stopping at the Dole Plantation in Wahiawa on the way for a pineapple soft-serve treat (~$6). Return to Waikiki around 10:00–10:30 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — start in Honolulu's Chinatown and Kalihi neighborhood. Visit Helena's Hawaiian Food (a James Beard Award winner) for kalua pig, lomi salmon, and poi. Then stop at Rainbow Drive-In for the classic plate lunch experience with two scoops of rice and macaroni salad.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Iolani Palace (the only royal palace on US soil, ~$22/adult, $6/child) for a fascinating family history lesson, then walk through the nearby Hawaii State Capitol grounds. Head to Ala Moana Beach Park for a relaxed afternoon swim — calmer waters than Waikiki, great for families.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ala Moana Center (one of the world's largest open-air malls) for souvenir shopping, then enjoy a sunset dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Café Kaila in Market City Shopping Center — famous for creative pancakes and eggs (~$14–18/person)
meals.lunch: Helena's Hawaiian Food or Rainbow Drive-In as part of the food tour (~$10–14/plate)
meals.dinner: Mariposa at Neiman Marcus Ala Moana (mid-range splurge, ~$25–40/person) or Genki Sushi at Ala Moana for fun conveyor-belt sushi (~$15–20/person)

day_by_day.notes: Helena's Hawaiian Food is closed on weekends — check current hours. The plate lunch food tour is self-guided and very budget-friendly. Ala Moana Beach Park has lifeguards and calm waters, making it ideal for younger children.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (HNL) to Maui (OGG) — short inter-island flight (~35 minutes, ~$60–100/person on Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest). Check into Maui hotel (recommendation: Aston at the Whaler on Kaanapali Beach or Hyatt Regency Maui, ~$200–280/night). Drop bags and head straight to the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — spend the afternoon on this iconic 3-mile stretch of golden sand. Rent snorkel gear (~$15/set) and explore the famous Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) snorkeling area at the north end of the beach. Watch cliff divers perform the traditional torch-lighting ceremony.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Kaanapali Beachwalk for sunset views. Enjoy dinner at one of the beachfront restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Airport grab-and-go or hotel breakfast upon arrival
meals.lunch: Hula Grill Kaanapali (beachfront, mid-range ~$18–28/person) — great fish tacos and burgers with ocean views
meals.dinner: Leilani's on the Beach at Whalers Village (~$25–40/person) for fresh seafood with stunning sunset views over the Pacific

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights at least 2 weeks in advance for best prices. Kaanapali Beach is consistently rated one of America's best beaches. The Black Rock cliff diving ceremony happens nightly at sunset — a free, memorable family experience. August brings calm west-facing waters ideal for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana scenic drive — depart early (7:00 AM) to beat traffic. Stop at Twin Falls for a short family-friendly hike to beautiful waterfalls (~30 min round trip). Continue to the Garden of Eden Arboretum (~$20/car) for lush tropical scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana, stopping at Wai'anapanapa State Park (advance reservation required, ~$5/person) for the famous black sand beach. Explore sea caves and dramatic coastal lava formations. Have a picnic lunch with pre-packed food.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Kaanapali (approximately 2.5–3 hours back). Fresher, less-trafficked return via the same route. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or Gazebo Restaurant in Napili (~$12–16/person) — famous for macadamia nut pancakes
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch (pick up supplies at Safeway in Lahaina the night before) enjoyed at Wai'anapanapa State Park
meals.dinner: Lahaina Grill or Mala Ocean Tavern in Lahaina (~$25–35/person) — note: check current status of Lahaina restaurants post-2023 fires; alternatives include Star Noodle in Lahaina

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is a full-day commitment — 620+ curves over 52 miles. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance online reservations (book 30 days ahead). Pack motion sickness remedies for children. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, water, and snacks. Note that parts of Lahaina are still recovering from the 2023 wildfires — be respectful when visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Maui (OGG) to Kona (KOA) on the Big Island (~45 minutes, ~$60–100/person). Check into hotel (recommendation: Courtyard by Marriott King Kamehameha's Kona Beach Hotel, ~$180–220/night). Head directly to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (approximately 1.5-hour drive from Kona — alternatively, fly into Hilo for a 45-minute drive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — visit the Kilauea Visitor Center for orientation, then walk the Kilauea Iki Trail (4-mile loop, moderate, ~2 hours) across a hardened lava lake. Drive the Crater Rim Drive for panoramic volcanic views. See the Thurston Lava Tube (Nahuku) — a family favorite.
day_by_day.evening: If lava is actively flowing or glowing (check NPS website), stay for the dramatic after-dark glow of Halema'uma'u Crater. Drive back to Kona or stay overnight near the park (Volcano House Hotel inside the park, ~$200/night, if pre-booked).

meals.breakfast: Airport or hotel breakfast before flying
meals.lunch: Volcano House Restaurant inside the park (~$18–25/person) with caldera views — a unique dining experience
meals.dinner: Jackie Rey's Ohana Grill in Kona (~$20–30/person) for fresh local fish and Hawaiian-inspired dishes

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park entry fee is $35/vehicle (valid 7 days). Check the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current eruption status before visiting. The park is at 4,000 ft elevation — bring a light jacket as temperatures are cooler. Children love the lava tube walk. Book Volcano House well in advance if staying overnight.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — visit Hapuna Beach State Recreation Area (one of Hawaii's best white-sand beaches, free entry) for a last family swim and snorkel session. The calm, clear waters are perfect for a relaxed farewell to Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kona town for last-minute souvenir shopping along Ali'i Drive. Visit the Kona Coffee Living History Farm or pick up 100% Kona coffee directly from a local farm store. Pack bags and head to Kona Airport (KOA) for the return flight to the mainland.
day_by_day.evening: Fly from Kona (KOA) back to LAX or connecting airport. Return to SureStay Hotel Buena Park if needed for an overnight before final travel home.

meals.breakfast: Lava Java Coffee Roasters on Ali'i Drive, Kona (~$10–15/person) — beloved local café with ocean views
meals.lunch: Da Poke Shack in Kona (~$12–16/bowl) — award-winning fresh poke, a perfect final Hawaiian meal
meals.dinner: Airport dining or back at hotel in Buena Park — BJ's Restaurant or similar for a comfortable end to the trip

day_by_day.notes: Hapuna Beach has lifeguards and excellent facilities — ideal for a final family beach morning. Allow at least 2 hours before departure for airport check-in at KOA. Purchase Kona coffee and macadamia nut chocolates as gifts — these are the best value Hawaiian souvenirs. Reflect on an incredible 10-day balanced Hawaii adventure!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 11:20 AM — Flight Alaska lands. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to hotel. Check in early if possible at SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the hotel and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park area. Visit a nearby spa or hotel pool to decompress after the flight. Pick up any last-minute travel essentials at a local shopping center.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at a premium local restaurant near Buena Park to celebrate the start of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Light snack or meal on the flight before landing
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or a quick premium bite at the airport upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Ranch Restaurant & Saloon (Anaheim) or a comparable upscale steakhouse near Buena Park — enjoy a hearty welcome meal

day_by_day.notes: No activities scheduled before 11:20 AM arrival. Focus Day 1 on rest and recovery. Confirm all Hawaii inter-island bookings and activity reservations this evening. Note: The hotel is in Buena Park, CA — Hawaii activities begin once you fly to the islands. Coordinate Hawaii-bound flights for Day 2 morning.

day_by_day.morning: Early checkout and private luxury transfer to LAX or John Wayne Airport for your flight to Honolulu, Oahu. Upon landing, check in to your luxury Waikiki resort (e.g., The Royal Hawaiian or Halekulani Hotel). Enjoy a welcome amenity and ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach for a gentle first afternoon in Hawaii. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas, take a beginner surf lesson with a private instructor, or simply wade in the warm Pacific waters with the family.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's oceanfront bar followed by a fine dining dinner with panoramic ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go premium breakfast at the Buena Park hotel or airport lounge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the resort upon arrival — try the poolside menu at The Royal Hawaiian's Mai Tai Bar
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Mer at Halekulani — Hawaii's most celebrated fine dining restaurant featuring French-Hawaiian cuisine with ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book early morning flights to maximize time in Honolulu. Pre-arrange luxury resort check-in to avoid wait times. Confirm private airport transfer in Honolulu. Weather note: August averages 16.8°C highs with some rain — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Depart early (7:00 AM recommended) to beat crowds at this protected marine sanctuary. Book a private guided snorkeling tour for the family with premium equipment provided. Explore the vibrant coral reef teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and colorful marine life in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the resort pool or beach. Optional: Book a private catamaran sailing cruise along the Oahu coastline for stunning views of Diamond Head.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Hawaiian luau — book the premium Paradise Cove Luau or Germaine's Luau for an authentic cultural experience with fire dancing, hula performances, and a feast.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast buffet before departing for Hanauma Bay — try the Surf Lanai at The Royal Hawaiian
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a premium Waikiki restaurant such as Duke's Waikiki — enjoy fresh fish tacos and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Full luau feast at Paradise Cove — traditional kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia dessert, and unlimited tropical drinks included

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations — book online at least 2 days ahead. Entry is limited to protect the ecosystem. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. Bring underwater cameras or rent GoPros for snorkeling. Luau typically runs 5:00–9:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — Depart by 9:00 AM for the 35-mile drive to Laie on Oahu's North Shore. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Participate in hands-on cultural activities like coconut husking, fire making, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Polynesian Cultural Center — watch the spectacular canoe pageant on the lagoon, enjoy cultural performances, and explore the IMAX theater. Upgrade to the Ali'i Luau package for a premium VIP experience with reserved seating.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the breathtaking 'HA: Breath of Life' evening show — a world-class theatrical production celebrating Polynesian culture with stunning costumes, acrobatics, and fire performances.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a wide spread of Pacific Island cuisine including Hawaiian, Samoan, and Tongan dishes
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau premium dinner at the Polynesian Cultural Center — traditional imu-roasted kalua pig, fresh seafood, and tropical desserts with VIP seating

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ambassador VIP package for the best experience — includes guided tours, priority seating, and exclusive access. The full day runs approximately 12:00–9:30 PM. Drive or arrange a private luxury shuttle. Great for families with children of all ages.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — Join a premium guided food tour of Honolulu's most iconic local eateries. Visit legendary spots like Rainbow Drive-In, Zippy's, and Helena's Hawaiian Food. Sample classic plate lunches featuring two scoops of rice, macaroni salad, kalua pig, lau lau, chicken katsu, and fresh poke.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chinatown Honolulu and the historic downtown area. Visit the Iolani Palace (the only royal palace on U.S. soil), browse the Honolulu Museum of Art, and stroll through the vibrant Chinatown markets. Optional: Book a private historical walking tour.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset hike or drive to Diamond Head State Monument for panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean at dusk, followed by a premium dinner back in Waikiki.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort — fresh tropical fruit, acai bowls, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Multiple tastings throughout the plate lunch food tour — a true feast of authentic Hawaiian comfort food
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nobu Honolulu — world-renowned Japanese-Peruvian fusion cuisine with premium sashimi, black cod miso, and signature cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book the food tour with a reputable local guide company for the best insider experience. Diamond Head hike is approximately 1.6 miles round trip — wear comfortable shoes. Sunset at Diamond Head is spectacular but arrive 1 hour before sunset for parking.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului, Maui (OGG) — book a short 30-minute inter-island flight. Check in to your luxury Maui resort (e.g., Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea or Andaz Maui at Wailea). Enjoy the resort's world-class amenities and stunning ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — Drive 45 minutes north to the legendary Kaanapali Beach. Spend the afternoon on this stunning 3-mile stretch of golden sand. Rent premium beach equipment, try stand-up paddleboarding, snorkel the famous Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a), or simply relax under a private cabana.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the traditional cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a Maui tradition performed nightly. Enjoy dinner at a beachfront restaurant in Kaanapali.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Honolulu resort or airport lounge before the inter-island flight
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Leilani's on the Beach at Kaanapali — fresh fish, burgers, and tropical cocktails with ocean views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Japengo at the Hyatt Regency Maui — premium Pacific Rim cuisine with fresh sushi, seafood, and stunning sunset views over Kaanapali Beach

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights on Hawaiian Airlines for the best service. Kaanapali Beach is consistently ranked among America's best beaches. The Black Rock cliff diving ceremony occurs nightly at sunset — arrive 30 minutes early for a good viewing spot. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Private Road to Hana luxury tour — Hire a private driver and luxury vehicle for the iconic Road to Hana experience. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, explore the lush Waikamoi Nature Trail, and marvel at the dramatic Wailua Falls. Enjoy exclusive stops away from the crowds with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana journey — visit the black sand beach at Wai'anapanapa State Park (book entry in advance), explore the Seven Sacred Pools at Ohe'o Gulch in Haleakala National Park, and take in the breathtaking coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort in Wailea for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a couples or family spa treatment at the resort's luxury spa, followed by a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — fuel up for the long day ahead
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort or stop at Coconut Glen's in Hana for legendary organic coconut ice cream and local snacks
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spago Maui at Four Seasons Wailea — Wolfgang Puck's signature California-Hawaiian cuisine with fresh local ingredients and ocean views

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 64 miles with 620 curves and 59 bridges — a private driver is strongly recommended for a premium experience. Book Wai'anapanapa State Park entry online in advance (required). Start early (7:00 AM) to avoid traffic. Bring motion sickness medication if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakala Sunrise Experience — Wake at 2:30 AM for a private luxury sunrise tour to the summit of Haleakala volcano (10,023 feet). Watch the spectacular sunrise above the clouds — one of the most awe-inspiring natural experiences in Hawaii. Bring warm layers as summit temperatures can drop to near freezing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by mid-morning and rest. After lunch, enjoy a premium whale watching or dolphin watching cruise (August may offer spinner dolphin sightings). Alternatively, book a private helicopter tour of Maui's dramatic coastline, waterfalls, and volcanic landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Maui dinner at one of the island's finest restaurants, celebrating the family's incredible experiences.

meals.breakfast: Light snacks and hot beverages provided during the Haleakala sunrise tour — enjoy a full resort breakfast upon return
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the resort — fresh salads, grilled fish, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mama's Fish House in Paia — Hawaii's most celebrated seafood restaurant, featuring the freshest locally caught fish with the fisherman's name on the menu. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise requires advance reservations through recreation.gov — book as early as possible as spots sell out months ahead. Dress in warm layers (temperatures near 0°C at summit). Mama's Fish House reservations should be made weeks in advance — one of Hawaii's most sought-after dining experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Maui (OGG) to Kona or Hilo, Big Island (KOA/ITO). Check in to your luxury Big Island resort (e.g., Four Seasons Resort Hualalai or Fairmont Orchid). Enjoy a brief resort orientation and morning swim in the resort's lava rock pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — Drive to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (approximately 1–2 hours from Kona or 45 minutes from Hilo). Witness the raw power of Kilauea, one of the world's most active volcanoes. Walk the Kilauea Iki Trail through a hardened lava lake, explore the Thurston Lava Tube, and view the glowing lava lake from the Jaggar Museum overlook.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. If lava is flowing to the ocean, arrange a premium lava boat tour or helicopter tour for a once-in-a-lifetime nighttime lava viewing experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Maui resort or airport lounge before the inter-island flight
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Rim Restaurant inside Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — enjoy panoramic views of the Kilauea caldera while dining
meals.dinner: Dinner at Beach Tree at Four Seasons Hualalai — elegant open-air dining featuring fresh Hawaiian seafood, wood-fired pizzas, and tropical cocktails on the oceanfront

day_by_day.notes: Check volcanic activity status before visiting — visit the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current conditions. Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for lava field walking. Bring a light jacket as the park sits at 4,000 feet elevation. Lava boat and helicopter tours must be booked in advance and are weather/activity dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — Enjoy a premium snorkeling experience at Kealakekua Bay, one of Hawaii's best snorkeling spots with abundant marine life and the Captain Cook Monument. Book a private kayak and snorkel tour for an exclusive experience. Alternatively, visit the stunning green sand beach (Papakolea) or black sand beach (Punalu'u) for a unique farewell to Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final lunch and leisurely afternoon. Pack, check out, and arrange a private luxury transfer to Kona International Airport (KOA) for your return flight. Browse the airport's local shops for premium Hawaiian souvenirs — Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, and Hawaiian sea salt.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Kona International Airport for your return flight to the mainland. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day Hawaiian adventure filled with world-class beaches, cultural immersion, volcanic wonders, and unforgettable family memories.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — indulge in a full Hawaiian breakfast spread with fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, Kona coffee, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Huggos on the Rocks in Kailua-Kona — casual yet premium oceanfront dining with fresh fish, lobster, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal — pick up premium local snacks and treats for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Kona Airport at least 2 hours before departure. Confirm all return flight details and arrange baggage handling for any purchased souvenirs. Consider shipping large purchases home via FedEx or UPS from the resort. Kona coffee is best purchased directly from local farms — ask the concierge for recommendations. Mahalo for an incredible Hawaiian journey!
